title: American Diabetes Association Fucked Up Real Bad Trying To Placate Trump Administration
text:
Failures

As we near the halfway point in the second Trump presidential term, there’s something that is worth remembering: Donald Trump, like most nasty viruses, is a temporary condition. Trumpism may not be, though I have my doubts as to how long a cult of personality can survive without that specific personality leading the cult. But Donald Trump as president will come to an end in the not too distant future.

The millions and millions of people who have been negatively impacted by him and by those who have decided to bow at his cultish altar, are not temporary. They are not going to go away. And they will remember the actions of many during this time.

And I imagine the American Diabetes Association, and specifically those currently leading it, will be in the memories of its members and many others for a long, long time. It’s been nearly a week since the ADA had five diabetes scientists, including its own former president, involuntarily removed from outside the ADA’s annual conference by police. Their crime? Distributing a copy of an editorial from the April edition of the ADA’s own journal.

The scientists were distributing the editorial outside the conference’s opening speech, which was originally scheduled to be given by Jay Bhattacharya, head of the National Institutes of Health under Trump. Bhattacharya canceled at the last minute, and senior NIH official Rick Woychik took his place.

Within minutes of beginning to hand out the editorial, police reportedly escorted the scientists out of the conference, which was held in New Orleans. The police reportedly shoved at least one scientist, took all of their conference badges, and threatened to arrest them if they tried to return. Louisiana State Police later told media that they acted at the request of the ADA. The ADA subsequently barred the five scientists from the rest of the conference.

The editorial just so happened to be very critical of the Trump administration and RFK Jr.’s funding at NIH and other health agencies and groups. It’s quite obvious that the ADA feared repercussions from the Trump administration if it wouldn’t allow these scientists to hand the article out while members of the administration were speaking and tried to use the police to silence them. And then, when this whole thing went viral, the ADA offered up justifications for its actions. Justifications that kept changing, as it turns out.

In an email to ADA members Saturday, the association said the scientists were removed because they didn’t have prior approval to distribute material at the conference and that it was “not because of the viewpoints expressed in those materials,” according to reporting from Science.

In a statement Sunday, the organization, which is a nonprofit, said it removed the scientists because it was complying with federal regulations for 501(c)(3) nonprofits, which requires “maintaining a strictly nonpartisan environment at all organizational events and functions while engaging across party affiliations to advance our mission.” However, the federal regulations do not restrict leaders of organizations from sharing political views in a personal capacity or from speaking on important public policy issues.

And from there, the Streisand Effect took over. The editorial, which you can find right here, went somewhat viral itself, getting a ton more attention than it had to date. But the real backlash came from the public and from within the medical community itself. There have been resignations in protest of the ADA’s actions. An open letter to the ADA signed by 40 members was written to torch leadership’s actions and treatment of the scientists at the conference. Another open letter was also written, likewise demanding an apology.

And, finally, the ADA did in fact apologize days later.

In the video Wednesday, ADA CEO Charles Henderson personally apologized to the five scientists, including Aaron Kelly, pediatrics professor at the University of Minnesota; Justin Ryder of Northwestern University; and Irl Hirsch, also of the University of Washington, in addition to Kahn and Schatz.

“What transpired is not reflective of who I am, the values I hold, or the way I was raised,” Henderson said. “I will work hard to bring our community back together to build on the progress we have collectively made for those affected by diabetes.”

In addition to apologizing to the five ejected scientists, Henderson apologized to the community as a whole, saying that the ADA would commission a “thorough independent review of the events that occurred as well as the policies, procedures, and decision-making process that guided our actions.”

Yeah, no, not good enough. The fish stinks from the head down, as the saying goes, and there have been days worth of attempts to make this stupidity anyone’s fault but leadership at the ADA. This was a clear attempt to lick the Trump administration’s boots, at the very moment when clear leadership from medical groups is so sorely needed, and that’s a bell that cannot be un-rung.

Henderson needs to go. And I have little doubt that he will before too long. Trump and RFK Jr. will eventually be gone, as well.

But we won’t forget how groups like the ADA, and the people leading them, acted during this time.

Filed Under: free speech, jay bhattacharya, nih, protests, streisand effect
	

	Companies: american diabetes association

See, you say things like ‘the people won’t forget’ but provide no mechanism to produce consequences.

If you want ‘the people won’t forget’ to be an actual threat, there needs to be a metaphorical fist behind it, or at least a metaphorical wet fart.

Right now ‘The people’ are a paper tiger. Fortunately, given his track record in court, so is Trump.

It’s real fucking pathetic watching two paper tigers have a slap fight for the history of the usa.

Right now ‘The people’ are a paper tiger. Fortunately, given his track record in court, so is Trump.

Given the courts’ track record concerning making anything stick, so are the courts.  And it doesn’t particularly help that the highest court of the land is thoroughly corrupted and exhibiting this to a degree where one has to wonder just what and who are in the unpublished parts of the Epstein files.

The number one rule for organizations who act stupid like this to remember is that you can’t unshit a bed.

the ADA had five diabetes scientists, including its own former president, involuntarily removed from outside the ADA’s annual conference by police. […] police reportedly escorted the scientists out of the conference, which was held in New Orleans. The police reportedly shoved at least one scientist, took all of their conference badges, and threatened to arrest them if they tried to return.

This is confusingly written, but makes it seem a lot like the scientists were removed from inside the conference. That is, from a private event rather than, for example, the sidewalk outside of it.

if so, apart from the brutality, the police would’ve been actly legally. That’s rather important information these days.

You are saying, it’s wrong for ADA conference attendees to distribute material from the ADA?

I have no idea how anyone could infer such a thing from the preceding message. It would be illegal to do that after being properly ordered not to (or to remain after being ordered to leave), which does not in any way suggest it would be wrong.

The cops removed them for, wait for it, distributing ADA material. The inference is, that they were removed from an ADA conference for distributing ADA material.

The cops removed them for, wait for it, distributing ADA material.

No, they didn’t. The cops removed them for trespassing; that is, being on private property after being ordered to leave by those currently renting it. The reason, if any, why the renters decided to give that order is not generally a matter of police concern (unless, for example, it’s illegally discriminatory under civil rights laws).

I don’t see anyone disputing the stupidity; the only question was whether the stupidity was being accurately described.

The cops removed them for trespassing; that is, being on private property after being ordered to leave by those currently renting it.

And why did the renters, who were in fact the ADA, ask those people to leave?

…although not a very large one, I’ve made my views known in no uncertain terms: I demanded that Henderson be publicly fired and publicly denounced.  It’s not enough to just ease him out the door with a quiet resignation: he needs to be humiliated and degraded in the same way that humiliated and degraded eminent scientists.  His “apology” is just another transparent lie and is worthless; it’s obvious to everyone that he couldn’t wait to drop to his knees and service Trump, even though doing so required betraying the core values of the ADA.

Enough.  Anyone who does this has to be removed, banned, blacklisted, ostracized.  Permanently.

I wonder what would have happened if the leadership at the ADA had simply admitted the truth, and said something like:

“We panicked…  We were afraid of how the Trump regime would react to this criticism — and in our desire to protect this fine organization and the hundreds of scientists and the millions of Americans that depend on its activities, we overreacted… We panicked and we responded in the worst way possible.

We let you down. Very badly. All the advocacy groups, all the researchers, and the millions of Americans who rely on us, we let you all down.

We were wrong. Very wrong. We lost sight of our principles, and we exercised bad judgement. We should have remembered those principles, that we all share, and acted with more courage. And perhaps most of all, we should have had more faith in our membership. We are ashamed and truly sorry for this failure, and we promise to do much better in the future.”

. . .

I don’t know how the thin-skinned, authoritarian-minded Trump/MAGA regime would have reacted to this — maybe even worse than the reaction that the ADA leadership feared and tried to avoid in the first place.  But we’ve seen how complying in advance works out (hint: it doesn’t).

Complying in advance is a losing strategy, even counter-productive one. So instead, give the American public something to believe in, and perhaps to rally around. In the longer view, plain speech and principled resistance is the only kind of response that will serve now.

Scientific facts are still partisan.  I understand why they reacted in that manner.

I’m not sure if I am being sarcastic or not…

I take exception to the first paragraph.
The thing you HAVE to remember is…

THERE IS NO UPSIDE TO HIM LEAVING OFFICE!

As long as he’s in office, he won’t be going to jail.
As long as he’s in office, New York State can’t provide a punishment for his 50-odd guilty counts in court. (member that? all procedings shut down when he became the nominee?)
He can’t be forced to pay that 80-odd million for his rape-and-slander of E. Jean Carroll.

And so on.

And so, I repeat, there is zero upside to tRump leaving office. Prepare now for the future.

THERE IS NO UPSIDE TO HIM LEAVING OFFICE!

Only when it comes to Trump. For literally everyone else, there is a massive upside: He won’t be president any more.

For literally everyone else, there is a massive upside: He won’t be president any more.

That’s not clear at all, because Vance would become president. Trump, at least, is inept, and prone to seemingly-random firings that might make it hard for the competent people succeed at the fascism they aspire to.

That’s not clear at all, because Vance would become president.

On one hand, he’s more competent than Trump.

On the other hand, he doesn’t have any real political instincts, any of Trump’s inexplicable charm, and any of Trump’s ability to bullshit his way through life. Vance as president would be bad, but it wouldn’t be worse than Trump because Trump is destructive and cruel to feed his ego, whereas Vance is a dumb asshole who would stumble along until the end of his time in the White House.

Donald Trump will not live forever. He will die sooner rather than later. There is serious question if he will make it to the end of his term. He is not the only person who wants power, and the vultures are circling. He is a temporary condition, and will depart the office in the not too distant future, one way or another.

Winston Smith was supposed to chuck that down the memory hole to avoid this embarrassment.

Uh, yeah, bro, it is, in fact, reflective of who you are.

So did Musk. The Tangerine turd is just biding his time before fucking Musk. He loves his revenge. I just wonder if Musk has enough brain cells to keep enough evidence to protect himself.

“But we won’t forget how groups like the ADA, and the people leading them, acted during this time.”

Sadly you are wrong about that. The public, especially a very select group of a certain political bent, are only too willing to forget what should have been unforgettable. They managed to forget McCarthy et al quickly enough to give us Reagan and Nixon and the Shrubs and Trump in rather short order.

From the American Diabetes Association itself (source link):

Chuck joined the ADA in January 2020 after spending 24-plus years in for-profit sectors and volunteering in the non-profit sector. Philanthropy and Sales/Fundraising are threaded through the fabric of his DNA. Chuck comes to the ADA from Champion Life Safety Solutions [fire sprinklers & etc in TX & OK] where he was CEO and President. Before that, he was a Field Sales Executive running multi-billion-dollar territories across the country for Dell Healthcare, Common ground Marketing (including executing special events in the field), and Viacom.
  […]
  Chuck is skilled in building trusted and collegial working relationships, relationship selling/fundraising, driving productivity, leading, and supporting change-management initiatives.

In other words, (imho, natch,) the guy’s the ADA’s CEO because he was bog-standard CEO material hired to run an org, not because he was ever a principled crusader for people’s health.

…In other other words, it should be no fucking surprise whatsoever that he bent the knee.

So there’s really no way that the American Diabetes Association can sugar-coat this?
